title: Technological, geographic and institutional influences

draft.title: Technological, geographic and institutional influences
card: These three influences come from outside a business. It cannot control them, but it must respond to them.
Technological
new tools and methods, such as online ordering or machines that automate work. They change what a business sells and how its work gets done.
Geographic
where a business is and what that place is like. Distance from suppliers and customers affects transport costs, and climate affects demand, such as for heaters or sunscreen.
Institutional
organisations that set and enforce rules. The ATO (Australian Taxation Office) collects tax. The ACCC (Australian Competition and Consumer Commission) enforces competition and consumer law.
draft.remember: Technology changes how and what. Place changes costs and customers. Institutions set the rules.

a.q: Which of these is an institutional influence on a business?
opts: The ACCC fining a shop for misleading advertising
A new app that lets customers book appointments online
High freight costs for a store in a remote town
A hot summer that lifts sales of electric fans
a.why: The ACCC is an organisation that enforces consumer law, so its fine is an institutional influence. The booking app is technological, while freight costs and a hot summer are geographic, because they come from location and climate.
a.clue: Look for an organisation that enforces rules.

b.q: Ella's ice cream shop in Cairns sells well because the weather is warm all year. She buys a new freezer that uses less power. Which influences are shown?
opts: Geographic and technological
Institutional and technological
Geographic and institutional
Technological only
b.why: Warm weather all year is climate, a geographic influence on demand. The new freezer is a new tool that cuts running costs, a technological influence. No organisation is setting or enforcing a rule, so nothing here is institutional.
b.clue: Is any organisation making Ella follow a rule?

a.best: The ACCC fining a shop for misleading advertising

problems.detail: The card defines geographic influence as 'where a business is' and says the business cannot control it. Point 6 of this chapter lists a business's location as part of the internal environment, which it can control. Students will meet a direct contradiction. Reword to something like 'the features of a place, such as distance and climate, that a business must respond to'.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer. The card says a business cannot control 'where a business is', which contradicts point 6, where location is internal and controllable, so the geographic line needs rewording.
